subject: HealthScale reserved capacity: clarifying workload/ GPU sizing for proposal
summary: Post-discovery follow-up to confirm dedicated/reserved capacity sizing inputs (TPS targets, token mix, latency SLO, GPU preference) and request for pricing/proposal.
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire O'Neil <c.oneil@healthscale.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: HealthScale - dedicated/reserved capacity pathway questions and next steps

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for carving out time today — really helpful to walk through the HealthScale clinical triage/summarization use case. Per our call, I wanted to capture a concise recap and a few clarifying asks so we can put together a recommended reserved-capacity proposal (SKU + rough cost + timeline).

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workloads: clinical notes summarization and frontline triage (short-form generation + classification).
- Must support long-context documents (up to ~8k tokens) for some flows.
- Latency target: p95 goal ~250ms for most interactive APIs.
- Data residency: US-only; HealthScale prefers VPC/private network for PHI-related endpoints (we discussed Private vs Dedicated tradeoffs).

Needed clarification (can you confirm / send samples):
1) TPS profile: baseline sustained TPS vs allowed burst (95th/99th percentile). If you can share typical minute-by-minute or hourly peaks that helps.
2) Token mix: average prompt tokens + average response tokens, and percent of requests that need full 8k context versus short context.
3) Peak request concurrency (how many simultaneous users/requests you expect at peak).
4) Exact latency SLOs by endpoint (triage vs summarization can have different targets).
5) Any hard constraints on GPU type (preference for H100 vs L40S/A10G) or budget guidance for reserved commits.
6) Timeline: when would you like the reserved pool provisioned (ASAP vs Q4)?

Attachments: I attached a quick template (poc_workload_sample.csv) you can fill with per-endpoint expected TPS, token mix, and peak concurrency. Also open to a quick follow-up call if that's easier.

Next steps (what we will do):
- Once you send the sample traffic, Marcus and Aditya will run a sizing exercise to recommend GPU type and number for a reserved pool (with burst autoscaling options).
- We'll return a short proposal (SKU + price bands + migration notes) and suggested canary rollout plan for HealthScale's staging + prod.

Would next Tuesday or Wednesday morning PST work for a 30-minute sizing sync?

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachment: poc_workload_sample.csv (template)
From: Claire O'Neil <c.oneil@healthscale.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthScale - dedicated/reserved capacity pathway questions and next steps

Hi Stephanie — great notes, thanks. Answers inline below and attached a sample of June traffic + our SOC2 questionnaire.

1) TPS profile: baseline sustained ~20 TPS for steady daytime traffic, with planned nightly batch windows. We see bursts up to ~65 TPS for short spikes (usually 30-60s duration) during peak clinic hours. 95th percentile sits around 45 TPS.
2) Token mix: average prompt ~=1200 tokens, average response ~=400 tokens. Roughly 22% of requests need a full 8k context window (long document uploads), the rest are short (<= 1k).
3) Peak concurrency: at peak we expect ~55 concurrent interactive requests (users hitting async endpoints for triage).
4) Latency SLOs: triage endpoints p95 <=250ms; summarization endpoints p95 <=350ms (we can tolerate slightly higher there).
5) GPU preference & budget: we care about predictable latency; ideally H100-class performance but we need pricing bands for H100 vs L40S. If H100 is cost-prohibitive, recommend alternatives.
6) Timeline: pilot in August, production reserved pool in early October.

Attachments: sample_traffic_june.csv, SOC2_questionnaire.pdf

If you can put together a short recommended reserved SKU range (minimum commit, recommended burst capacity, and expected latency profile per SKU) that would be great. We can iterate after your sizing calc.

Thanks — Claire
Claire O'Neil
Head of Product, HealthScale
claire.oneil@healthscale.ai
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire O'Neil <c.oneil@healthscale.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HealthScale answers + traffic (sizing ask)

Aditya / Marcus — forwarding Claire's email and attachments. Key constraints: p95 triage <=250ms, ~22% long-context 8k requests, baseline 20 TPS with 65 TPS bursts, peak concurrency ~55. They prefer H100-class latency but need cost comparisons (H100 vs L40S). Pilot Aug -> prod Oct.

Can you each take an action:
- Aditya: run a quick capacity model for two scenarios (conservative: target p95 <=250ms with H100s; cost-sensitive: L40S with slightly higher p95). Please include: estimated GPUs required (initial reserved + burst headroom), expected concurrent request handling per GPU (with suggested batching/kv-cache settings), and notes on memory/KV sizing for 8k contexts. A one-sheet with assumptions is fine.
- Marcus: prepare 2 pricing bands (monthly reserved cost) for the recommended SKU counts, plus notes on minimum commit and expansion cadence. Also include canary rollout recommended steps (staging -> prod) and expected lead times for provisioning.

We should aim to send HealthScale a short proposal by EOD Monday (my timezone PST) so they can review before next week's planning meeting.

Thanks — Stephanie

Quick preliminary sizing (high level) — will follow with an attached spreadsheet (initial_capacity_modeling.xlsx):

Assumptions
- Model family: 70B-class chat model with quantization-friendly execution path (approx token/step cost modeled after Llama-variant benchmarks).
- Avg token work per request = prompt 1200 + response 400 = 1600 tokens. Long-context requests assume KV cache hit + 8k context processing on first request.
- Target p95 latency <=250ms for triage; we budget slightly higher cycles for summarization.

Scenario A — H100 focused (low-latency):
- Single H100 host (multitenant) sustained throughput estimated ~8–10 TPS for 1600-token average with p95 ~200–250ms depending on batching.
- With aggressive batching and KV cache, effective concurrency per H100 roughly 8–12 in steady-state; burst headroom with autoscale recommended.
- To cover baseline 20 TPS steady + handle 65 TPS bursts, recommend initial reserved pool of 3 H100s + configured burst autoscale to 6 H100s. This yields headroom for spikes and staged canary testing.

Scenario B — L40S cost-sensitive (balanced latency):
- Single L40S host estimated ~5–7 TPS for 1600-token average at p95 ~300–400ms depending on batching and kernel optimizations.
- For tighter p95 we need more parallelism; recommend initial reserved pool of 5 L40S with autoscale to 8 for bursts.

Notes on 8k contexts and KV cache:
- For 8k-context first-pass requests, memory footprint grows; we recommend ensuring each host has at least 80–100GB GPU memory equivalent for near-peak contexts (H100 preferred for this workload). KV caching reduces repeated cost for sequential interactions — configure a per-session KV TTL for clinical flows.

Next steps: I'll attach the modeling workbook with detailed per-host throughput numbers and cost ranges. Marcus — please use these SKU counts to draft two pricing bands and commit options.

Aditya Rao
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Attachment: initial_capacity_modeling.xlsx
